statement: R0 shows no detection->Z effect mainly because detection bypasses Z
decision: Measured, not inferred: ||dL_det/dZ|| is exactly 0 in R0 at all three widths and >0 in R2. The R0 null was the bypass.

statement: Once detection is forced through Z, mAP becomes clearly Z-sensitive
expected_evidence: monotone or clearly separated mAP50 across z
decision: Detection Z-sensitivity rises to 2.34x noise (mAP50) and 2.56x (mAP50_95), but it is not monotone: z16->z32 is 0.14x noise, only z16->z128 clears the floor.

statement: z=16 is already sufficient for DA
expected_evidence: DA spread across z stays inside the noise floor
decision: DA spread is inside the noise floor in BOTH R0 (<=0.30x) and R2 (<=0.61x). Saturation is real, not a bypass artefact.

statement: Lane's Z demand is real, not R0-specific training noise
expected_evidence: lane_fg rises with z again, reproducing the Phase 3B trend
decision: lane_fg z16->z128 is 2.25x noise under R2 versus 1.00x under R0. The lane Z demand reproduces and strengthens under a shared bottleneck.

statement: Encoder-heavy still beats Z-heavy under a genuine shared bottleneck
expected_evidence: wider encoder + narrow Z beats narrow encoder + wide Z
decision: Phase 3C settled this under R0 only. No encoder sweep was run under R2, so the allocation law is not yet known to transfer.

statement: Compressing encoder features into Z causes irreversible information loss
experiment: R2 vs R0 at equal z
expected_evidence: R2 detection below R0 detection at every z
decision: No dead channels at any width, and detection IMPROVES through Z, so compression to z>=16 is not measurably lossy here. What is lost is effective dimensionality, not task performance.

statement: R2 performance depends as much on reconstruction design as on Z width
expected_evidence: two reconstructions differ at fixed z=16
decision: Only one reconstruction (DetFromZ, det_ch=32) was trained. Its contribution cannot be separated from Z width without a second design.

statement: A single Z can serve all three tasks
expected_evidence: R2 approaches R0 on all three tasks at wide z
decision: A single Z does serve all three tasks, but not optimally: detection and lane want z128, DA is indifferent at z16. It works, it is not ideal.

statement: Tasks need different granularity, so one uniform Z is suboptimal
expected_evidence: task-specific projection beats direct heads at fixed z
decision: Task-specific demand is measurable: detection 2.34x, lane 2.25x, DA 0.21x noise over the same z16->z128 range.

statement: Task gradients conflict at Z and shape how it is used
expected_evidence: negative cosine between task gradients w.r.t. Z
decision: Cosines are ~0 (det-da -0.002..+0.001, det-lane ~0.000, da-lane +0.033..+0.060). Tasks are near-orthogonal, not in conflict, so conflict does not explain Z insensitivity.

statement: Extra Z capacity is allocated but not used
expected_evidence: effective rank of z128 close to that of z16
decision: Utilisation falls from 42.5% of channels at z16 to 24.9% at z128 (effective rank 6.79 -> 31.93 of 16 -> 128), so most added channels are redundant. Caveat: none are dead and the redundant ones still buy real gains (detection 2.34x, lane 2.25x noise), so it is low-utilisation, not pure waste.

statement: Bottleneck placement matters more than width
expected_evidence: moving compression point changes results at fixed z
decision: Only one bottleneck placement was trained (Z at 1/8 resolution, compression before all three heads). Width was swept, placement was not, so the two cannot be compared yet.
